content:
Carla Mendes: Hey team, day 1 here. Followed the kube quickstart but `kubectl get ns play` replies "namespaces "play" not found". I'm pretty sure the doc uses `play` namespace. I used the Okta SSO flow and my kubeconfig shows two contexts. Any tips?

Jayden Park: welcome Carla! :wave: Quick runbook: 1) `kubectl config current-context` 2) `kubectl config get-contexts` 3) `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n play`. Paste outputs if you can.

Carla Mendes: `kubectl config current-context` -> `redwood-dev`. `kubectl config get-contexts` ->
```
CURRENT   NAME            CLUSTER            AUTHINFO
*         redwood-dev     gke-redwood-dev    carla@okta
          redwood-ci      gke-redwood-ci     ci-sa
```
But `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n play` -> no. Also `kubectl get ns` lists default and kube-system only.

Jayden Park: sounds like RBAC. Two ways we do this for new hires: grant a namespaced RoleBinding to your Okta principal or give you a short-lived service-account token for the team SA. RoleBinding is faster for interactive work. Do you want to be unblocked quickly or learn the SA flow now?

Carla Mendes: unblock me quickly please. I'll switch to SA token later for CI.

Jayden Park: copying infra. @eng-infra-bot can you open an INFRA ticket to grant `carla@okta` `edit` in `play`? TTL 24h ok.

eng-infra-bot: Created INFRA-5023: "new-hire Carla Mendes - play ns access". Assignee: @platform-oncall. ETA 1h.

platform-oncall: Hi Carla 44b I can apply a RoleBinding now. Quick question: do you need namespace-scoped volume mounts or clusterroles for the tutorial? I can limit to `edit` if not.

Carla Mendes: just needs to run the sample pods and tests, no cluster-wide perms. Edit is fine.

platform-oncall: Applied namespaced RoleBinding (edit) for `carla@okta` in `play`. Try:
```
kubectl auth can-i list pods -n play
kubectl get pods -n play
```

Carla Mendes: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n play` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n play` -> lists 5 demo pods. Yay, thanks! :tada:

Jayden Park: nice. If you want the SA flow later, here's a short snippet we recommend (k8s >=1.24):
```
# get ephemeral token from team SA
kubectl create token dev-team-sa -n play
# set a local kubeconfig user/context
kubectl config set-credentials play-sa --token="$(kubectl create token dev-team-sa -n play)"
kubectl config set-context play-sa-ctx --cluster=gke-redwood-dev --user=play-sa --namespace=play
kubectl config use-context play-sa-ctx
```

Jayden Park: note: tokens from `kubectl create token` are ephemeral; for long-lived automation talk to infra about our secrets service and projected service account tokens.

Carla Mendes: saved that. Two follow-ups: 1) how do I avoid accidentally using the CI context? 2) where do I mark this step done?

Jayden Park: 1) create a minimal alias: `alias kplay='kubectl --context=redwood-dev --namespace=play'` or use a dedicated kubeconfig for onboarding. 2) onboarding checklist is ONBOARD-250, I'll link the INFRA ticket.

platform-oncall: Linked INFRA-5023 to ONBOARD-250 and marked the K8s access step pending your confirmation.

onboarding-bot: ✅ K8s access granted. INFRA-5023 -> ONBOARD-250.

Carla Mendes: marked ONBOARD-250. Thanks everyone for the quick help :heart:
